standard_prerequisites.name: Classical Fourier and Sobolev analysis
standard_prerequisites.statement: Plancherel, Fourier/Laplace inversion, Sobolev embedding and trace on a line, weighted-moment equivalence, Young and Schur estimates, interpolation, and elementary commutator/Leibniz formulas.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local Hartree well-posedness and continuation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For each fixed hbar in(0,1], the weighted quantum Sobolev data have a unique maximal self-adjoint solution with persistence of regularity; bounded lower Sobolev control on each finite interval gives continuation. This is the standard local input explicitly invoked by the source at761 and860, not a claimed new local well-posedness proof.

core_obligations: Derive the uniform linear Volterra control and close both parts of the nonlinear density norm, including the hbar-weighted extra derivative and resonant shrinking-cylinder response kernel.

Exploit self-adjointness and quantum commutator cancellation to close the five coupled density/profile norms, choosing bootstrap constants before a sufficiently small perturbation size uniformly in hbar.

Propagate the strict improvements globally using the explicit local continuation input and prove absolute time-integrability of both Duhamel contributions in the lower quantum Sobolev norm, yielding the stated scattering rate.

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the profile, differentiated equation, parameter hierarchy and global bootstrap framework.
Obtain the resolvent derivative/decay control used by linear damping.
Close the two density norms, including the extra hbar-weighted derivative.
Close high and low profile energies and pointwise Wigner control using cancellation and the selected hierarchy.
Recover density decay and integrable Duhamel tails for scattering.

difficulty_reason: Even with the previously prepared Schur integrals available, the nonlinear theorem requires the additional hbar-weighted density derivative, self-adjoint quantum cancellation, an ordered five-norm bootstrap closure, and a lower-regularity scattering argument. These nonlinear estimates do not follow from the old linear phase-mixing theorem or the Penrose criterion.

compared.difference: Old primary is the linearized density/scattering theorem; it removes the quadratic interaction [w*rho_Q,Q]. The target retains this interaction and proves global nonlinear control uniform in hbar.
The two uniform response-kernel integrals are included uncounted support. Nonlinear quantum energy cancellation and all other bootstrap closures remain additional work.
Penrose is a hypothesis here; this target does not count another sufficient linear-stability criterion.

The original classical screened Vlasov mechanism is credited. The target is the quantum Hartree equation with the hbar-weighted density derivative and constants uniform in the semiclassical parameter.

dedup.scope: Current source/claim metadata, same-source current P tasks, inherited2538 and existing exact BMM comparison record in the Schur task; no broad claim of proof-mechanism novelty.

editorial_notes: Only the full nonlinear main theorem is counted. Bootstrap improvements, Green-function bounds, resonance integrals and the scattering deduction are solution components, not separate new tasks.

Local well-posedness/persistence and its continuation criterion are explicitly permitted standard inputs, following the authors declaration at761 and860. The uniform nonlinear a-priori closure is fully supplied.
The Penrose boundary criterion and sufficient radial/smallness cases are outside this task; uniform Penrose stability is an assumption.

The original bootstrap dependency diagram is native TikZ in the selected proof and needs no external raster asset. Bibliography keys are mechanically mapped to the publishers exact references; the BMM and Nguyen-You attribution is retained.
